body:
Coils are the part of a vape that wears out first, and knowing when to replace one is the difference between a device that tastes good every day and one that slowly turns flat, harsh or burnt without you noticing. There is no single number of days that applies to every coil, because life depends on the liquid you use, the power you run, how you puff and how well you prime and look after it. This guide explains what happens to a coil over time, gives realistic ranges, lists the signs that a coil is worn, shows how liquid, power and habits shorten or extend life, explains how to plan replacements and spares, what it costs over a year and how to fit a new coil properly. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice.

## What happens to a coil over time
A coil heats liquid again and again, and every puff leaves a little residue. Sugars, sweeteners and other components from the liquid bake onto the heating surface and into the cotton. Over days, that residue builds up, and it does three things: it insulates the coil, so that heat spreads less evenly; it clogs the cotton, so that liquid wicks more slowly; and it adds its own taste, which is the flat, muddy or burnt note you eventually notice. The metal itself also ages with heating cycles. A coil that has done its work is not broken, it is simply spent.

## Realistic ranges
As a rough guide, coils last from several days to a few weeks. Pod coils in closed pods are usually replaced with the pod, often every week or two for regular use. Tank coils, for refillable tanks, often last one to three weeks. Mesh coils tend to be consistent for much of their life and then drop off, while some wire coils fade more gradually. Heavy users, high power and sweet liquids sit at the short end. Light users, moderate power and cleaner liquids sit at the long end. Treat these as ranges, and let the signs below decide.

## Signs a coil is worn
- **Flavor fades or goes flat,** even with fresh liquid.
- **A burnt or harsh taste** that appears even when the wick is wet.
- **Vapor thins,** with weaker clouds or a cooler draw.
- **Gurgling or leaking** that keeps returning, because the cotton no longer wicks properly.
- **A dark, crusty or gunky look** on the coil, where it can be seen.
- **The device needs more power** to give the same result.

One sign on its own may have another cause, such as a low battery or empty liquid, so rule those out first. Two or more together, with a fresh fill and a charged battery, point to a worn coil. See [why a vape tastes burnt](/blog/vape-tastes-burnt/) and [vape flavor fading fixes](/blog/vape-flavor-fading-fixes/).

## What shortens coil life
### Sweet and thick liquids
Dessert, candy and heavily sweetened liquids leave more residue, and high-VG liquids can be slow to wick through small coils. These are the biggest reasons coils wear faster than expected. If you love sweet flavors, plan for more frequent replacements.

### High power
Running above the coil's recommended wattage burns cotton and bakes residue quickly. Stay in the middle of the range, or lower. See [ohms, watts and volts](/blog/what-are-ohms-watts-and-volts-in-vaping/).

### Chain vaping
Rapid puffs do not give the wick time to re-saturate, so the coil runs dry and scorches. Take breaks between puffs.

### Skipping priming
A new coil that is fired dry can be damaged at once. See [how to prime a new coil or pod](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/).

### Low liquid
Letting the tank or pod run low dries the wick. Refill before it is nearly empty.

### Heat and neglect
Leaving a device in a hot car, or not cleaning residue from the tank, shortens life.

## What extends coil life
- Prime every new coil properly.
- Use liquid suited to the coil, with the right PG/VG ratio. See [PG and VG ratios](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/).
- Keep power in the lower half of the range.
- Take steady puffs with breaks.
- Keep liquid above the minimum.
- Store the device upright, cool and clean.
- Rotate flavors, so that very sweet ones do not use up the coil first.

## How to plan replacements
Note the date you fit each coil. After a couple of coils, you will know your own average. Buy replacements before the current one is finished, so that you can swap at the first sign of wear. Keep one spare on hand. For a device used daily, a pack of several coils usually lasts one to two months. Buy a new pack when you open the last coil but one.

## A worked cost example
Suppose a pack of five tank coils costs $10, so $2 each. If each lasts about ten days, you need about three a month, costing about $6, or about $73 a year. If you switch to a less sweet liquid and lower the power so that each coil lasts fourteen days, you need about two a month, costing about $4, or about $52 a year. Replacing on time, rather than pushing a spent coil, costs little and gives better flavor. For pods at $4 for two, replaced every ten days, the cost is about $12 a month. Compare these running costs with disposables when you decide what to use. See [how to compare vape prices per puff](/blog/how-to-compare-vape-prices-per-puff/).

## How to replace a coil
1. Switch the device off and empty the tank, if it is refillable, or remove the pod.
2. Unscrew the old coil, or remove the pod.
3. Check the contacts and the base for liquid and residue, and wipe with a dry cotton bud.
4. Unpack the new coil, avoiding the cotton.
5. Drip a few drops of liquid on the cotton, and fit the coil firmly.
6. Fill the tank or pod below the line, and let it rest for five to ten minutes.
7. Start at low power with gentle puffs, and increase gradually.

See [how to change a pod or coil](/blog/how-to-change-a-pod-or-coil/) for a fuller walkthrough, and [how to pick replacement coils and pods](/blog/how-to-pick-replacement-coils-and-pods/) to choose the right part. Dispose of used coils at a recycling site with your devices; see [how to dispose of vapes and batteries](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/).

## Disposables
You cannot replace the coil in a disposable. Its life is the life of the device. Gentle use and good storage help it last. When flavor fades and liquid is finished, replace the whole device.

## Common mistakes
- **Waiting for the coil to taste burnt** before replacing it.
- **Not keeping a spare.**
- **Skipping priming.**
- **Using very sweet liquid and expecting long coil life.**
- **Running maximum power.**
- **Buying the wrong coil for the device.**

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Can I clean a coil to make it last?
Not reliably. Dry burning or soaking can damage a coil and electronics. Replace it.

### Do more expensive coils last longer?
Sometimes, but life depends mostly on use. Compare real-world reviews.

### Why did my coil last only three days?
Probably sweet liquid, high power or chain vaping. Adjust one thing at a time.

### Should I replace a coil when I change flavor?
Not necessarily, but strong residue from a previous flavor can ghost. Many users keep a coil for one flavor family.

### How do I know the new coil is fitted properly?
It seats firmly, the device fires and the resistance reading, if shown, matches the coil.

## Shop
Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A replacement schedule you can follow
Start by assuming about ten days for a tank coil and about a week for a pod, then adjust. Write the fit date on a sticky note on the device. When flavor starts to fade, note how many days it has been, and adjust your schedule to that number minus a day or two, so that you replace before the taste drops. After two or three coils, you will have a figure that suits your liquid and habits. Keep one spare for the day it falls early.

## Spotting the right moment
Replace when the first puffs of a session taste muddy, not when they taste burnt. Many people leave coils far too long because the change is gradual, and the new coil is a revelation. A good test is to keep a fresh coil aside and compare it with the old one for a few puffs. If the difference is large, you waited too long. The cost of replacing slightly early is a few cents, and the benefit is flavor every day.

## Coils and different liquids
If you use more than one liquid, treat flavor families separately. A coil used with a heavy dessert liquid will carry residue that a later fruit liquid will pick up. If you rotate widely, replace the coil when you change families, or keep a coil for each family. If you stay with one flavor, a single coil will last as long as the liquid allows. See [vape flavor fading fixes](/blog/vape-flavor-fading-fixes/) for ghosting.

## When replacement does not help
If a fresh coil tastes burnt, the cause may be the liquid, the power or the priming, not the coil. If a fresh coil leaks, the seals or the tank may be at fault. If a fresh coil fires but gives no vapor, check the contacts and the battery. Work through the checks in [why a vape is not hitting](/blog/why-is-my-vape-not-hitting/), and change one thing at a time.

faq.q: How often should I replace a coil?
faq.a: As a rough guide, from several days to a few weeks, depending on liquid, power and use. Let the signs decide.

faq.q: What are the signs of a worn coil?
faq.a: Flat or burnt flavor, thin vapor, recurring gurgling or leaking and a dark, crusty coil.
Sweet and thick liquids, high power, chain vaping, skipping priming and letting liquid run low.

faq.q: How many spares should I keep?
faq.a: At least one, and a pack of several if you use the device daily.

faq.q: Can I replace the coil in a disposable?
faq.a: No. Disposables are sealed. Replace the whole device when it is finished.
